rounds.text: The most significant risk facing Vama Wovenfab Ltd is the disconnect between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation. While the company reports strong profitability, it suffered a negative cash conversion of -0.50x in March 2026 [E20]. This is underscored by an operating cash flow of Rs -6 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -7 Cr for the same period [E21, E22]. Furthermore, the company’s reliance on external funding is increasing, with borrowings rising to Rs 29 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 25 Cr the previous year [E24]. The stock’s momentum is also concerning, as it currently sits at only 9% of its 52-week range, suggesting significant downward pressure [E5]. Additionally, despite reporting repeated profits, the company provides no dividend yield to shareholders [E4, E37]. Conceded: the company maintains strong return metrics, including a 3-year median ROE of 46% and a discounted cash flow model suggesting a high margin of safety [E16, E29].
